BERT4Rec’s original paper explicitly appends a reserved [MASK] at inference and includes training examples masking only the final item to reduce the training–inference mismatch. Terminal-mask alignment therefore has established precedent. Mask-proportion experiments favored 0.6 for Beauty, 0.4 for Steam, and 0.2 for MovieLens; these concern overall masking density, not a controlled ablation of terminal-example allocation. [Original paper, §§3.6, 4.6](https://arxiv.org/html/1904.06690)

The official generator creates `dupe_factor` randomly masked copies plus one terminal-only copy per sequence/window, then shuffles them together. With `dupe_factor=10`, explicitly terminal-only examples constitute 1/11 of generated examples, excluding incidental terminal masks in random copies; this is not their share of supervised targets. Training adds these examples even with `force_last=False`; `force_last=True` selects evaluation construction using the latest sequence window. Contexts come from complete short histories or deterministic sliding windows, rather than uniformly sampled prefix endpoints. `masked_lm_prob` controls target selection, whereas `mask_prob` controls replacement with [MASK]; the supplied MovieLens script sets them to 0.2 and 1.0, respectively. [Official generator](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/gen_data_fin.py), [run script](https://github.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/blob/master/run_ml-1m.sh)

Increasing terminal-example allocation or sampling prefix endpoints should consequently be framed as a modification of established training construction. The paper’s one-mask comparison does not isolate terminal-allocation effects. Local baseline behavior remains unverified and requires separate documentation; upstream code cannot establish its sampler, target weighting, or masking probabilities. [Original paper, §4.4](https://arxiv.org/html/1904.06690)
